L34: ###

L36: Paper Submission Requirements and Instructions
L37: 
L38: CoRL is double-blind, which means all papers must be anonymized. The accepted papers and reviews will be publicly accessible and de-anonymized after decisions are announced. Our aim is to have at least two reviewers per paper. Accepted papers will appear in the cite9†Proceedings of Machine Learning Research†proceedings.mlr.press (formerly JMLR Workshop and Conference Proceedings).
L39: Please keep in mind that the deadlines are final, and we cannot make any accommodations for missing the abstract deadline or paper deadline. Authors may update the title and abstract on OpenReview after the abstract submission deadline. However, authors cannot be added or removed after this deadline, as this information is required to facilitate reviewer assignments. If you need to request an exception, please email our OpenReview Chair cite10†Carlo Sferrazza†sferrazza.cc (csferrazza@berkeley.edu).
L40:   * Papers may be submitted through OpenReview via the link cite11†here†openreview.net (https://openreview.net/group?id=robot-learning.org/CoRL/2026/Conference). All submissions should comply with the format and length indicated below:
L41:   * Page limit will be 8 pages for the main paper. Acknowledgments, References, and Appendix (optional) will not count towards the page limit. Please note that reviewers are not required to read the Appendix. The Appendix can be included with the main paper or with the Supplement.
L42: 
L43:   * Please use the LaTeX template: cite12†here†drive.google.com (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1R9irIW0ImqeDHh5g8Ukm2XGy91sWxOsQ/view?usp=drive_link ).
L44:   * Authors are encouraged to submit a supplementary file containing further details, which the reviewers may decide to consult.
L45: 
L46:   * Authors are highly encouraged to submit a video not exceeding 250 MB (strict) and not more than 3 minutes in length (suggested), providing an overview of the work.
L47: 
L48:   * All supplementary materials will be submitted through OpenReview as a single zip file.
L49:   * All accepted papers will be presented in poster sessions, while selected papers will be invited for an oral spotlight presentation.
L50: 
L51:   * All submissions should include a Limitations section (counted toward the 8-page limit), explicitly describing limiting assumptions, failure modes, and other limitations of the results and experiments, and how these might be addressed in the future.
L52:   * Authors are strongly encouraged to include all relevant details in the main paper and the appendix to ensure that future researchers can reproduce the methodology and results.
L53: ###
L54: 
L55: Submission Policy
L56: 
L57: We will not accept papers that are identical or substantially similar to papers that have previously been published or accepted for publication in an archival venue, nor papers submitted in parallel to other conferences or archival venues. Archival venues include conferences and journals with formally published proceedings, but do not include non-archival workshops. Submission is permitted for papers that have previously appeared only as a technical report, e.g., in arXiv.
L58: Dual submission policy: Dual submission is not allowed by default. Submissions that are simultaneously under review at another archival venue will be desk-rejected without review. However, we recognize that some conferences may have decision timelines that slightly overlap with our review period (e.g., ICML decisions on May 1st). In such cases, authors must notify the Publication Chair before submission and clearly indicate the overlapping venue and relevant dates.
L59: Approval for such exceptions will be granted on a case-by-case basis. Failure to disclose dual submission may result in rejection and may be reported to both venues.
L60: Generative AI policies: We understand that generative AI is a useful tool in the paper writing process. In order to ensure that the use of generative AI does not pose an undue burden on the review process, we are implementing the following policies this year:
L61: 
L62:   1. Papers that contain citations to references that do not exist will be desk-rejected after review by the Program Committee.
L63:   2. Authors must take full responsibility for the content in submitted papers. LLMs or other generative AI tools do not qualify for authorship. During the paper submission process, authors will be asked to briefly disclose how generative AI tools were used for research and paper writing.
L64:   3. Authors who submit multiple versions of substantially the same paper (e.g., different papers with the same method, but slightly different ablations, baselines, or algorithmic variations) will face desk rejection of all papers they have submitted, and potentially also be prevented from submitting papers to future iterations of the conference. We are aware that generative AI tools have been used for this purpose in recent conferences, and we will implement checks to flag such papers.
L65: With these policies, we aim to strike a balance between beneficial uses of generative AI (e.g., help with paper editing, figures, literature review, or brainstorming) and uses that degrade the overall quality and integrity of the peer-review process.
L66: CoRL 2026 has partnered with GPTZero to detect references that do not exist in academic databases in all submitted papers. Please refer to GPTZero's cite13†technical report†gptzero.me regarding the system for details. All flagged citations were manually checked by Area Chairs, Senior Area Chairs, and Program Chairs before recommending desk rejection of papers.
L67: ###
L68: 
L69: Reciprocal Reviewing Requirement
L70: 
L71: Qualified authors are required to review for CoRL, according to the policies below.
L72:   * All submissions must include at least one author who agrees to serve as a CoRL reviewer. They are qualified if they have at least one accepted publication at a previous robotics (CoRL/ ICRA/ IROS/ RSS) or learning conference (ICLR/ NeurIPS/ ICML) or equivalent journal.
L73: If none of the authors are qualified under this definition or all authors are exempt (e.g., serving as AC or SAC), then they are exempt from this requirement.  The abstract submission form will allow submitters to designate an author to fulfill this requirement or to indicate that the submission is exempt from the requirement.
L74:   * Additionally, every author with 3 or more submissions must agree to serve as a reviewer. Authors are exempt from the review requirement if they serve as an AC, an SAC, or another organizing chair for CoRL 2026.
L75:   * Submissions that do not meet this reciprocal review requirement may be desk-rejected. Additionally, reviewers who fail to adequately participate in the review process (e.g., not submitting reviews on time or submitting highly insufficient or inappropriate reviews) may have their own submissions desk rejected. The program chairs may grant exceptions on a case-by-case basis.
L76: ###
L77: 
L78: Rebuttal Process
L79: 
L80: In order to focus reviewer effort, papers that do not receive at least one score of weak accept or above from either a reviewer or the Area Chair will be candidates for first-round rejection without rebuttal. Senior Area Chairs and Program Chairs will review all such candidates before any decision is finalized.
L81: Authors of all other papers are invited to submit a 1-page rebuttal in pdf by the rebuttal deadline. You will not be able to give individual responses to the reviewer on OpenReview, nor will you be able to update the paper during the rebuttal process. The rebuttal should be focused on addressing any factual errors in the review.
L82: All rebuttals will be reviewed by the reviewer, the original AC, and, if applicable, external reviewers. The AC reserves the right to invite new reviewers if needed. The results of the current review(s) will be shared with the new reviewers in such cases.
L83: ###
L84: 
L85: Concurrent/contemporaneous Work
L86: 
L87: We consider papers contemporaneous if they are published within the last 4 months, so authors do not need to compare their own work to that paper. Authors are encouraged to cite and discuss all relevant papers, but they may be excused for not knowing about papers not published in peer-reviewed conference proceedings or journals, which include papers exclusively available on arXiv.
L88: ###
L89: 
L90: Camera Ready Paper Submission
L91: 
L92: New this year — additional page for incorporating reviewer feedback
L93: 
L94: Congratulations again on getting your paper accepted to CoRL 2026!  The camera-ready version of your paper is due by Oct 12, 2026 (23:59 cite14†Anywhere on Earth†www.timeanddate.com ). Please submit your camera-ready PDF and signed permission form through OpenReview.
L95: 
L96: Here are the instructions for preparing and submitting your camera-ready paper:
L97: 1. The camera-ready paper should follow the template: 9-page main text + acknowledgment + references + appendix (optional). Note that this year, we are allowing an additional page to accommodate feedback from the review process. The appendix should be included at the end of the camera-ready PDF, rather than as a separate file. cite15†The template is available here†drive.google.com . Please make sure to use “\usepackage[final]{corl_2026}.
L98: 2. One important note: PMLR does not allow videos to be submitted as supplementary material.  If you have videos, code, datasets, and other supplementary materials, please host them on your own (e.g., YouTube, GitHub, etc). You should provide, in the main text of your paper, a link to this material or a link to your project website.
L99: 
L100: 3. Please sign the permission form for publication in PMLR (cite16†form available here†proceedings.mlr.press ). Please rename the pdf to <paperid_firstname_lastname>.pdf.
L101: Please ensure:
L102: 
L103: 1.    Paper length: 9 pages main text + Acknowledgement + References + Appendix (optional)
L104: 
L105: 2.    The author list is NOT anonymous.
L106: 
L107: 3.    Footer on the 1st page: "10th Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026), Austin, Texas, USA."
L108: 
L109: 4.    Text density, fonts, and spacing should be the same as the provided template on the website.
L110: 
L111: 5.    The margin should be the same as the provided template on the website.
L112: 
L113: 6.    The OpenReview title is the same as the PDF title.
L114: Please contact Yoonchang Sung (yoonchang.sung@ntu.edu.sg) if you have any questions.

L119: Please note that the paper submission deadline is Thursday (5/28) EOD rather than Friday! We hope you enjoy your weekend after the deadline ;)

L7: Robotics: Science and Systems, 2027 welcomes Science and Systems papers that report on novel scientific and systems contributions. As always, we solicit your best work. This year, we are introducing new elements to the review and publication process. With the goal to rebalance our publishing structure toward long-term scientific progress and insightful, reproducible methodologies, we are implementing several structural changes, detailed below.
L8:

L10: ## Important Dates

L23: ## The Two-Stage Shepherding Process
L24: 
L25: RSS 2027 replaces the traditional single-deadline submission and rebuttal process with a two-stage development cycle to encourage engaged research shaping. This revised structure aims to preserve human involvement and oversight, despite the expected use of LLMs. Additionally, incorporating multiple decision stages acts as a cascading filter, allowing the Program Committee to sustainably manage a potentially unprecedented volume of submissions.
L26:   * Stage 1 (Initial Submission): Authors submit a 6-page Extended Abstract consisting of up to 5 pages of content and 1 page of references. We expect this Stage 1 submission to be a semi-complete paper; while the problem statement, hypotheses, and methodology must be fully fleshed out, it is expected that experiments or empirical validations will be missing or preliminary.
L27: The core of the manuscript must lay out the proposed methods, detailing the insights to be gained (even in the event of negative results). Due to the strict content limit, the related work section should cite only literature directly tied to the paper’s central problem and novelty. Reviewers will evaluate citations based on direct relevance rather than comprehensiveness at this stage.
L28: Authors are expected to provide a complete, comprehensive related work section, alongside their finalized experiments, during the Stage 2 final submission. Any additional content beyond the 6-page paper (e.g., websites or appendices) will not be considered for review. Extended Abstract submissions must be submitted by December 4th, 2026.
L29:   * Shepherding & Metareview: Reviewers and Area Chairs (ACs) will evaluate the paper’s hypothesis and methodology. Papers that are invited to proceed to Stage 2 will receive a Metareview, which outlines the required clarifications, evaluations, and methodological extensions required for the final paper. Authors can respond to this feedback during the rebuttal period (February 5 – February 12).
L30: Based on the authors’ response, the ACs will revise the Metareview into a finalized Extension Charter, which will be sent to the authors on February 26.
L31:   * Stage 2 (Final Submission): Authors will have until April 16 to execute the Extension Charter and finalize the paper. Before final acceptance, the Program Committee will review the final submissions to ensure that the Charter was followed and that scientifically valuable insights were achieved. Submissions will not be rejected for yielding negative experimental results.
L32: Rigorously falsifying a hypothesis is considered a valuable scientific contribution, provided the authors extract meaningful insights from the outcome.
